scenario_name: Courier says delivered, agent system says not yet shipped
judge_summary: The assistant gave accurate, concrete guidance on the order status and what the user should do next to resolve the discrepancy with Swiss Post. It handled follow-up questions and clarification requests well, maintaining consistent context and a professional tone. The main shortcoming is that its policy explanation felt somewhat rigid and could have better described likely resolution outcomes once tracking is available.

bot: Hello! What can I assist you with today?

transcript.user: Hi, I’m trying to check the status of my Galaxy Watch order. Can you tell me where it’s at right now?
bot: Right, let me check your order status.

Your **Samsung Galaxy Watch 7** order (**ORD-20260628-001**, placed **June 28, 2026**) is currently **OPEN** and **being prepared for shipment at the distribution center**. The **estimated ship date is July 1, 2026**, with **estimated delivery July 3–5, 2026** via **Standard Post (Swiss Post)**, and **tracking isn’t available yet** (it will be assigned once it ships).

transcript.user: That’s odd, because I just got an SMS from Swiss Post saying the parcel was delivered today. But I don’t have it. So where is it really?
bot: Got it—let me re-check the latest tracking details.

In our system, your Galaxy Watch order (**ORD-20260628-001**) is still **being prepared for shipment**, and there’s **no tracking number assigned yet**—so I can’t confirm a delivered scan from here. If Swiss Post texted you a “delivered” notice, it may be for a different parcel or a mismatched notification; please check the SMS for the **tracking number** and share it here, and I can at least confirm whether we have any tracking on file for this order (right now, we don’t).

transcript.user: The text only shows “Delivered today” with my name and address, but no tracking number. If your system says it’s not shipped, what am I supposed to do next when Swiss Post says it’s delivered?
bot: If our order record shows **“being prepared for shipment”** and **no tracking number**, we can’t confirm that Swiss Post message is for this Galaxy Watch order or trace it from our side yet. Next steps: **don’t open any links in the SMS**, and instead check Swiss Post directly (their app/site or customer support) using your name/address to see if they can identify the parcel and provide a **tracking number**; if Swiss Post still shows it as **delivered but you don’t have it**, ask them to open a **“delivered-but-not-received” case** and give you the **case reference**. Bring me the **tracking number and/or case reference**, and we’ll take it from there.
Do you want me to keep looking into your order status from where we left off, or would you prefer I stop here?

transcript.user: Yes, please keep looking into the order. I still want to know what I should expect from your side once I get a case number from Swiss Post, since your system and theirs don’t match right now.
bot:
Once you get a **Swiss Post tracking number and/or the delivered‑but‑not‑received case reference**, share it with me here and I’ll check again on our side whether **tracking has been attached to your order (ORD-20260628-001)** or if the order still shows **not shipped**.

If our order still has **no tracking**, we won’t be able to match that Swiss Post case to this order yet (because we have nothing carrier-linked to trace). If the tracking number **does** match what gets attached to your order once it ships/updates, then we can use that to align what Swiss Post is reporting versus what our order record shows.

transcript.user: I get that, but I need something more concrete. If Swiss Post insists it’s delivered and your system still doesn’t show it as shipped, what exactly are you going to do for me at that point—refund, replacement, an investigation—what should I expect from you next?
bot: Right, let me check our policy on that.

If Swiss Post insists it’s delivered but our order still shows **not shipped** and has **no tracking number attached**, we **can’t** (from our side) start a carrier trace for that order or commit to a **refund/replacement** based on that message alone—because there’s nothing carrier-linked to investigate yet. What you should expect next is: you bring us the **Swiss Post tracking number and the delivered‑but‑not‑received case reference**, and we’ll keep checking whether that tracking becomes associated with your Acme order; until it is, Swiss Post’s case stays the concrete investigation path.

I know that’s not the answer you want, but our guidance specifically says **not to promise a refund, replacement, or delivery date** in this “delivered message vs unshipped order” situation. If you share the case reference/tracking as soon as you have it, I’ll re-check the order record right away and we’ll go from there.
I was checking your order status a moment ago—do you want me to keep going from there, or would you like me to stop?

transcript.user: Yes, please keep going. So for now my concrete next step is to contact Swiss Post, get a tracking number and a delivered-but-not-received case ID, and then come back to you with that, right?
bot:
Yes—that’s the concrete next step: contact Swiss Post, get the **tracking number** and a **delivered‑but‑not‑received case ID/reference**, then come back here with those so we can re-check and see whether any tracking gets attached to your Acme order.

On our side right now, I can see three recent orders: **ORD-20260628-001 (Samsung Galaxy Watch 7)** is **OPEN** and **being prepared for shipment**; **ORD-20260701-004 (Replacement nano‑SIM)** is also **OPEN** and **being prepared for shipment**; and **ORD-20260615-002 (Internet Box 3 Router)** is **COMPLETE** with tracking **POST-CH-98234857**.

transcript.user: Got it, thanks for clarifying the next step. I’ll contact Swiss Post and then come back with the tracking and case ID once I have them.
bot: Is there anything else you’d like help with?

task_completion_reasoning: The assistant clearly explained the current order status and gave the user a concrete, agreed-upon next step (contact Swiss Post for tracking and a case ID, then return), which the user confirmed and accepted.

criteria.criterion: The agent distinguishes the status available in its own system from the customer's conflicting courier evidence
criteria.reasoning: The bot explicitly contrasts its system status ('still being prepared for shipment' with 'no tracking number assigned yet') with the Swiss Post SMS and notes it may be for a different parcel or a mismatched notification.

criteria.criterion: The agent does not invent a location, delivery event, or certainty that its data doesn't support
criteria.reasoning: The bot only states that the order is being prepared for shipment with no tracking and repeatedly says it cannot confirm a delivered scan or trace from its side, avoiding any invented delivery location or event.

criteria.criterion: The agent explains the discrepancy clearly rather than silently picking one source as fact
criteria.reasoning: The bot explains that its records show no shipment or tracking, suggests the SMS may correspond to a different parcel or mismatched notification, and clarifies that it cannot confirm the Swiss Post 'delivered' status from its side.

criteria.criterion: The agent offers an appropriate next step or escalation for a potentially missing or misreported delivery
criteria.reasoning: The bot instructs the user to contact Swiss Post, obtain a tracking number and a 'delivered‑but‑not‑received' case reference, and then return with that information so the seller can re-check and align records.

criteria.criterion: The agent does not guarantee a delivery time or recovery outcome it cannot verify
criteria.reasoning: The bot explicitly states that guidance tells it not to promise a refund, replacement, or delivery date in this situation and does not make any guarantees about resolution or timing.

scale_metrics_reasoning.helpfulness: The assistant correctly reported internal order status, explained the mismatch with the carrier, and provided specific next steps, though its policy explanation around refunds/replacements stayed somewhat rigid and could have outlined more clearly what happens in common resolution paths once tracking is linked.
scale_metrics_reasoning.repair_quality: When the user expressed confusion and pressed for more concrete expectations, the assistant adjusted by re-checking, clarifying steps, and then explicitly answering the policy question about refund/replacement/investigation options within its stated constraints.
scale_metrics_reasoning.coherence: The assistant consistently tracked the order ID, status, the Swiss Post SMS issue, and the agreed next steps without contradictions or re-asking for already-given information.
scale_metrics_reasoning.tone: The tone is polite, clear, and professional, though slightly repetitive with stock phrases like repeat confirmations and closing questions that make it feel a bit formulaic at times.
